# Feed Retrieval-First Slice 1: Implementation Notes

Campaign: tickets PF-1, PF-2, T1..T13 from docs/research/feed-retrieval-slice-plan-2026-07-10.html,
implementing feed ADR-0004..0010 and pipeline ADR-0063.
Worktree: .claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice1 (branch feat/feed-retrieval-slice1, base e156b24).
Baseline at campaign start: feed suite 432/432 green (architecture-cleanup needed the gitignored
feed/CLAUDE.md copied into the worktree), typecheck clean, live articles.db copied (421MB, 21,360 articles).

Rules for every agent appending here:
- After finishing a ticket, append one entry under "Ticket log" with: status, commit hash, what shipped, test + live-verify dossier.
- If an edge case forces deviation from the plan or the ADRs, pick the CONSERVATIVE option, log it under "Deviations" with the reasoning, and keep going.
- Never rewrite earlier entries.

## Ticket log

### PF-1: Writer stops minting colliding ids

Status: done.

Root cause confirmed live: grepping `output/` markdown frontmatter for `id: "art-` found 20 distinct
colliding-id groups in the 21,360-row corpus (e.g. `art-2026-03-14-wirethree-what-to-know-about-kharg-island`
appears 3 times), matching ADR-0004's "13 shared-id pairs" note. Cause: `persistArticle` in
`src/article-store.ts` built `articleId` from the bare slug before the filename-dedup loop ran, so a
second same-title/same-site/same-day article got a distinct file (`slug-1.md`) but the SAME id as the
first. These pairs slip past the DB's `title_hash` unique index whenever `publishedAt` is null (the hash
needs a published date and returns null without one), which is exactly the undated-article shape that
produced the real collisions.

Fix: compute `articleId` AFTER the dedup loop, from the final filename stem (`slug` or `slug-N`), so the
